artworks.title: John Selden
artworks.description: The image shows an engraving of a man's bust-length portrait, facing the viewer with a slight turn of the shoulders. The man has a high forehead, prominent nose, deep-set eyes, a mustache, and long wavy hair styled with a middle parting falling to his shoulders. He wears a dark robe or cloak and a white collar is visible. An oval frame with intricate patterns surrounds him, with an emblem or coat of arms on the right. The background has a lined pattern text below the portrait, presenting formal information typical of period engravings.

artworks.title: John Selden
artworks.description: This  is an engraved portrait of a man's upper body facing forward with his head slightly turned to the right. He has a long, narrow face with prominent cheekbones, a long nose, and a thin-lipped mouth. The man's eyes are deeply set under heavy brows. His wavy hair falls just past his shoulders. He is wearing a high-collared garment with draped fabric. There are no visible jewelry or objects. The background features a textured, engraved oval border with an inscribed scroll below the oval, containing the text "JOANNES SELDENUS" followed by additional cursive script.

artworks.title: John Souter, Merchant at Exeter
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait of a man named Mr. John Souter. He is shown from the upper half of his body, positioned slightly to the right with his head facing forward. The man has long, curly hair, a high forehead, arched eyebrows, and a slight smile. He is wearing formal attire from the 17th or 18th century, including a white cravat and a dark coat. The portrait is within an oval frame with a textured background, typical of engravings. A label below the portrait reads "Mr. John Souter."

artworks.title: John Whitgift, D.D., Archbishop of Canterbury
artworks.description: The image displays a portrait of an individual identified as Dr. John Whitgift. He is depicted from the chest up, facing forward inside an ornate oval frame. Dr. Whitgift has a prominent nose, a full beard, and a mustache. He wears a dark cap, ruffled collar, dark robe, and an undergarment with a decorative neckline. The background consists of horizontal lines, and the frame includes scrollwork and a decorative cherub above the subject's head. Below the figure, a plaque identifies the individual as "The most Reverend Dr. John Whitgift Ld. Arch-Bishop of Canterbury" with a coat of arms.

artworks.title: Benjamin Woodroffe, R.R.S., Canon of Christ Church, Oxford
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man facing slightly to the right. He has shoulder-length grayish wavy hair and a high forehead. The man is wearing a dark robe with a white collar. The portrait is in an ornate oval frame with decorative scrollwork. Below the frame is a coat of arms with a crest featuring a horse-like figure and floral elements. The background has a textured pattern.

artworks.title: Title Page to The Life of Faith by Richard Baxter
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a religious theme illustrating "The Life of Faith." The image features an intricate diagram divided into three main sections marked "Fide," "Spe," and "Charitate," translating to "Faith," "Hope," and "Charity." The central focus is a large oval with the Latin words "DEO PATRI FILIO SPIR S." Flanking the oval are two figures, one carrying a child and the other holding a staff. A banner at the top reads "The Life of Faith Per Christum." The oval is segmented into sectors representing virtues necessary for a life of faith, with smaller figures and Latin inscriptions depicting their actions and virtues. Various religious symbols are present, and cloud patterns suggest a divine presence. The image appears designed for educational and religious purposes, balancing line, and text to convey a solemn message.

artworks.title: Title Page to Gilbert Burnet, Historie of theReformation of the Church of England
artworks.description: This is a drawing of the reformation of the Church of England. The image depicts an elaborate allegorical scene featuring architectural structures and symbolic actions against elements like "Superstition" and "Religion." Figures are engaged in activities on two sides; on one, individuals are dismantling or confronting structures labeled as "Superstition," while on the other, they appear to be building or maintaining a structure under the banner "Religion." The scene is set within an architectural framework with decorative columns and a grand arch adorned with a banner displaying the event's title. Symbols of authority and scripture are present, indicating a rich religious and political context.

artworks.title: Queen Elizabeth
artworks.artist: Pieter van der Banck after Edward Lutterell
artworks.description: The image is a bust portrait of Queen Elizabeth. She is positioned facing slightly to the right but looking directly at the viewer. She has an elaborate hairstyle adorned with curls and wears a crown on top of her head. Her facial features include a composed expression with gentle eyes. Elizabeth is dressed in a richly decorated gown featuring a high lace collar, commonly known as a ruff, and a bodice adorned with intricate detailing and pearls. She is also wearing a pearl necklace and drop earrings. The portrait is set within an ornate oval frame featuring ribbons and crown motifs, which is further surrounded by a decorative border with floral patterns and leaf designs. At the bottom of the frame, there is an inscribed plaque with the name "QUEEN ELIZABETH" and a coat of arms. The background is a detailed decorative engraving.

artworks.title: Roger Assham and Mary Surrounded by MedallianPortraits
artworks.description: The image features a central scene with two figures within an ornate architectural setting. The figures are shown within a historical setting and wear elaborate costumes characteristic of the Elizabethan era. The background includes architectural details and decorative stonework. Surrounding the central scene are portraits of historical figures with names inscribed below each.

artworks.title: Sir Thomas Bodley, Founder of the Bodleian Library
artworks.description: The image shows a man standing from the waist up. He is facing forward with his left arm resting on his waist. He has strong facial features, a pointed mustache and beard, and short groomed hair. The man is wearing an ornate garment with a high collar and a cloak, with a sword at his side. Surrounding him are smaller portraits of four other men, each depicted head and shoulders. These men also have distinctive facial hair and wear period clothing. The background includes decorative borders and Latin inscriptions.

artworks.title: Thomas Bodley
artworks.description: The image is an engraving featuring multiple portraits, with the central figure showing a three-quarters view of a full-length male figure. The man stands with his body slightly turned to the side, gazing outward. He has short hair and a pointed beard, with finely arched eyebrows and a prominent mustache. He wears an intricate outfit consisting of a detailed doublet and layered garb, including a wide cloak draped around his shoulders, embellished with a wide ornate collar. In his left hand, he holds a sword. Surrounding the central figure are four smaller portraits, each framed separately. These depict different men, each dressed in historical garments characterized by high collars and substantial ruffs; some have distinctive headwear. The top of the image includes text inscribed within a box above the central figure. The background features a striped pattern within framed borders, with decorative seals incorporated into the panels.

artworks.title: Thomas Bodley
artworks.description: The image shows two medallions. The left medallion features a man in profile, facing right, with a beard and short wavy hair. He wears a high-collared garment. The text reads "TH. BODLY.” The right medallion shows a person standing in profile facing right, wearing a long tunic with a sash, holding two small busts. The person stands on a textured ground with text framing the medallion. Both medallions have a background of fine lines and decorative borders, with a horizontal line connecting them and a number “2” between them on the paper.

artworks.title: Thomas Bodley
artworks.description: The image shows a rectangular engraving with two circular medallions surrounded by intricate detailing and floral embellishments. On the left is a profile portrait of a man, shown from the shoulders up, looking to the right. He has a prominent nose, a beard, and short, wavy hair, wearing a high-collared garment. The medallion is encircled by text. On the right, the second medallion depicts a figure dressed in a classical robe, facing left and holding a mask in their right hand. This medallion is also bordered by text. Between the two medallions is a decorative section with scrolls, leafy vines, and a central cherubic face. The background features delicate floral and abstract scroll patterns, enhancing the intricate design.

artworks.title: Robert Eglesfield, Founder of Queen's College, Oxford
artworks.description: This is an engraved portrait of a person shown from the upper body up. The individual has a serious expression, detailed facial features, and is wearing a cap with a wide brim and a thick, high-collared cloak. The portrait is framed within an oval border and below it, there is an elaborate crest featuring three birds enclosed by ornate designs and Latin inscriptions "ROBERTVS COLL. REGINÆ ANNO EGLESFIELD FVNDAVIT MCCCXL." The background has a textured pattern without discernible objects or scenery.

artworks.title: William Somner, Anglo-Saxon Scholar and Antiquary
artworks.description: This is a portrait engraving of a man within an oval frame. The man has long, dark hair, a mustache, and a neutral expression. He wears a dark garment with a wide collar and a cravat or necktie. His right hand is visible on the edge of the frame. The frame is decorated with the name "SOMNERUS GULIELMUS," a face motif, and a dark, textured background. Below the frame is a plaque with the inscription "MORIBUS ANTIQUIS," a heraldic crest, and the artist's signature, M. Burghers.

artworks.title: Title Page to A New System of Mathematicks, Composed by Sir Jonas Moore, Knight
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a gathering of individuals engaged in mathematical study. The image depicts a scene of people sitting around a large globe, engrossed in scientific study and discussion. They are using telescopes, geometric tools, and are surrounded by charts and books. Above them, two figures sit on pedestals, holding a spherical astrolabe and other celestial instruments. The scene is framed within an ornate decorative arch. Below the main gathering, there are various mathematical instruments and books laid out.

artworks.title: Edmund Grindal, Archbishop of Canterbury
artworks.description: The image shows a man seated with an open book held in front of his chest. He has a long beard, a receding hairline, and is dressed in attire suggestive of a cleric or scholar. The man is framed by an intricate oval design and below the portrait is a heraldic shield with a Latin inscription identifying him as Edmund Grindall. Lines engraved in the background emphasize the oval frame and the subject.

artworks.title: Chronologer William Parsons
artworks.artist: Simon Gribelin II after Pierre Berchet
artworks.description: An engraving showing the upper body of a person in an upright pose. The person has a full, voluminous hairstyle framing their face. They have stern eyes and a neutral expression. They are wearing traditional attire from the late 17th century with draped fabric and a button or brooch. The person is surrounded by an ornate oval frame with a ribbon at the top indicating the year 1696 and an inscription at the bottom. The engraving features decorative elements and symbols against a plain background, emphasizing the central figure.

artworks.title: Sir Christopher Wren, Architect
artworks.description: The image is an engraving featuring the profile view of a man from the upper chest upwards. The man is in a seated position, facing left, with distinct facial features, curly hair, and formal clothing. The background is detailed with etching lines, and the portrait is framed in an octagon. Below it, there is a coat of arms and a text that reads “Sr. Chrisr. Wren K.” A Latin phrase at the bottom reads "Numero Pondere et Mensura."

artworks.title: Charles I and His Supporters
artworks.description: The image shows a structured and symmetrical arrangement of bust-length portraits. In the center is the largest portrait of a man in armor with curled, shoulder-length hair and a mustache, surrounded by a decorative oval laurel frame. Surrounding him are fifteen smaller, octagonal portraits of men with various hairstyles typical of the period. The men wear different period-appropriate attire and most have mustaches or beards. Each portrait is labeled with names in text boxes of different fonts and styles. The background is plain to emphasize the detailed portraits and attire.

artworks.title: Henry Bennett, Earl of Arlington
artworks.description: The image depicts a man's upper body facing the viewer with his right side slightly turned forward. He has curly hair falling over his shoulders and distinct facial features. The man has a serious expression and is wearing elaborate clothing, including a robe with detailed embroidery, a lace collar, cuffs, and a large chain around his neck. He is holding a scepter or staff in his right hand and wearing a badge or medallion on his chest. The background is a textured, draped cloth and there is decorative text with a coat of arms below the image.

artworks.title: Thomas Cartwright, Puritan Divine
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man visible from the chest up. He is depicted in a seated position straight towards the viewer. The man has prominent facial features with a long, pointed beard and a mustache. He is wearing a skullcap on his head, which covers his hair. His clothing consists of a dark robe with a fur-lined collar and a garment underneath that features buttons. The background is plain. The name "MR THO: CARTWRIGHT" is inscribed below the portrait.

artworks.title: Charles I
artworks.description: The image depicts an illustration of a man from the chest up, in profile facing to the right. The man has facial features including a prominent nose and a mustache and goatee. His hair is long and wavy, reaching his shoulders. He is clad in an elaborate garment with fur lining the collar. The background consists of concentric oval lines and the bottom of the image includes an inscription identifying the subject as Charles I, King of Great Britain, France, and Ireland.

artworks.title: Charles I
artworks.description: This image depicts a detailed engraving of a man from the chest up. The man is facing slightly to the right in a three-quarter profile position. He has long, wavy hair that falls past his shoulders and a pointed beard and mustache. His facial features include a long, narrow face with a prominent nose and contemplative eyes. He is wearing a garment with a high lace collar decorated with intricate patterns. Around him is an ornamental oval frame with flowing ribbons and leaves, and at the top, the words "CHARLES THE I." are inscribed in the frame. The background consists of closely spaced lines, adding texture to the engraving.
